summary: Both I and III have the inherited intransitive trembling meaning. Morphological III is not automatically causative: whole people and body parts are subjects, with no separately caused trembler. Active-shaped L-suffixed marʕele/marʕalle contrasts with I Preterit Intransitive raʕəl/Raʕili.

m- marks a cause such as fear, a dream or a loud cry. In the inherited III 90/48 example, l ǧəsm diḏe marks a body domain; 90/59 places ǧəsm dəṯṯe before marʕalle. The available transcription leaves some subject-versus-body-domain relations open.
Contracted ruʕli/rəʕli and feminine ruʕlo/rəʕlo retain root l. In komarʕli/komaraʕli, plural -i follows that root consonant; do not parse a first-person patient solely from final li.

kroʕəl is I Infectum with a collective masculine people subject, not an L-coded experiencer or a caused trembler. The absence of an explicit m-cause does not alter the existing sense.
